components.purposeStatement: A single collapsible disclosure section whose header row toggles a body region; use to progressively reveal one optional block of content. NOT for navigation, tabs, or modals, and NOT for a static grouping surface (use Card).

antiPatterns.pattern: <div> + onClick toggling visibility with inline padding/border/radius to fake a collapsible header and body
antiPatterns.reason: re-invents the disclosure surface and hardcodes spacing/border/radius literals, drifting from the token scale and skipping accessible expand/collapse semantics

components.purposeStatement: Shows the user's position in a navigational hierarchy as a row of ancestor links ending in the current page; NOT for primary site navigation, tabs, or stepping through a linear wizard.

antiPatterns.pattern: A hand-rolled row of <a> tags joined by a literal '/' or '>' character with ad-hoc margins
antiPatterns.reason: Re-invents the trail with raw separators and off-token spacing, drifting from the registered crumb spacing, type scale, and current-page treatment.

components.purposeStatement: Horizontal single-select group of 2-4 equal-width segments for mutually exclusive option/view switching; NOT for route navigation, binary on/off (use Switch), multi-select, or triggering actions (use Button).

antiPatterns.pattern: A row of styled <button>/<Button> elements toggling a 'selected' class to fake a segmented control
antiPatterns.reason: Re-invents an existing registered component with ad-hoc selected styling and inconsistent radius/spacing.

antiPatterns.pattern: Using two <Switch> or several <Badge> elements to express a single mutually-exclusive choice
antiPatterns.reason: Wrong semantics — these do not enforce single-selection and drift from the canonical control shape.

components.purposeStatement: A compact, axis-less inline trend line/bars summarising one stat's direction at a glance; NOT a full readable chart with axes/labels and NOT a static status pill (use Badge).

antiPatterns.pattern: An inline <svg> with a raw hex stroke and px width/height to draw a tiny trend line next to a number
antiPatterns.reason: Bypasses the token system and the registry, re-inventing a one-off chart that drifts in colour and sizing

antiPatterns.pattern: Adding axis ticks, gridlines, value labels, or tooltips to convey precise readings
antiPatterns.reason: A sparkline communicates direction only; precise reads belong to a full chart component

transforms.rule: cssVar = '--' + id, with each dot→'-' and camelCase→kebab. e.g. color.action.primary → --color-action-primary; fontSize.md → --font-size-md; space.md → --space-md
scalar tokens become a CSS custom property and a `token.<path>` accessor that returns 'var(--…)'
composite → applied via <Text variant>; not a single var
composite → single --shadow-<name> css var with the assembled box-shadow string

swift.target: DS enum namespace + Asset Catalog colors + ShapeStyle/Font extensions

transforms.rule: applied via .dsType(.<seg2>) modifier or Font.ds<Cap seg2>

decisionLog.justification: Swift codegen emits scalar tokens (DS.Spacing/Radius/...) and semantic Color extensions but not composite shadow primitives, so the .dsShadow(_:) modifier encodes shadow.{sm,md,lg} values directly. These literals are encapsulated in ONE token-layer file and are the single source for swift shadows — downstream code references .dsShadow(.md), never the raw values.
decisionLog.remediation: extend codegen.js to emit a DS.Shadow representation; then DSShadow.swift references it.
